title: Symphony No. 94 in G major, “Surprise”
hook: A quiet tune, a little quieter, then a crash: Haydn’s most famous joke.

painting.title: Vauxhall Gardens
painting.collection: Yale Center for British Art, New Haven
painting.pairingNote: London’s concert-going crowd at an evening concert in the 1780s, busier looking at one another than at the orchestra: the public Haydn set out to catch off guard.
painting.medium: Watercolour, pen and black and grey ink, and graphite on laid paper

facts: Haydn wrote the symphony in London in 1791, on the first of his two visits to England. It was first played on 23 March 1792 at the Hanover Square Rooms, with Haydn directing from the keyboard. It is the second of the twelve symphonies he wrote for London.

The famous surprise comes in the slow movement: a simple tune is played softly, then even more softly, and is cut off by a loud chord from the whole orchestra with a stroke on the timpani. In German the work is called the symphony “with the drumstroke”.

A popular story says Haydn wanted to wake up listeners who dozed through slow movements. Haydn’s own explanation, given years later to his biographer Griesinger, was that he wanted to surprise the public with something new, so that his former pupil Ignaz Pleyel, whose rival concerts had begun a week earlier, would not outshine him.
The premiere audience greeted the slow movement with great enthusiasm. Haydn later reused its tune in his oratorio *The Seasons* (1801), where a ploughman whistles it.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a gentle introduction and a bustling dance (I), the surprise and its variations (II), a minuet too fast to dance (III), a racing finale with drums (IV).

movements.heading: Adagio cantabile – Vivace assai
movements.summary: A short, gentle slow introduction leads into a quick movement in [[sonata-form|sonata form]] with a skipping, dancing rhythm. The fast music starts almost in a whisper before the whole orchestra bursts in.

mainIdeas.name: The introduction
mainIdeas.description: slow, singing phrases passed between woodwinds and strings.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: a quick, light tune in a rocking six-beat rhythm that starts quietly in the strings.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a graceful, lilting tune in a new key.

stops.hear: Slow, quiet phrases, woodwinds answered by strings
The violins start a quick, skipping tune very quietly; then the whole orchestra bursts in
A lighter, more graceful tune
The quiet skipping tune again
The skipping tune breaks into pieces and moves through new keys
The opening of the Vivace returns

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: Loud, firm chords from the whole orchestra

notice: Haydn begins the fast music softly, so the first loud entry of the whole orchestra has extra force. It is a smaller version of the trick in the next movement.

movements.heading: Andante
movements.summary: A simple tune and four variations on it: in each [[variation|variation]] the tune stays, but something around it changes. Everyone knows what is coming; the trick still works because the tune is so innocent and so quiet.

mainIdeas.name: The theme
mainIdeas.description: a simple, nursery-rhyme tune in short, detached notes, first in the strings.

mainIdeas.name: The surprise
mainIdeas.description: one loud chord for the whole orchestra, with the timpani.

stops.hear: The strings play a simple, detached tune quietly; the lower strings pluck
The tune is repeated even more quietly; then a loud chord from the whole orchestra, with a drum stroke
The tune again, with a quick, decorative line above it in the first violins
Suddenly loud and in the minor, with trumpets and timpani
stops.happening: Variation 2, in C minor: the stormiest variation

stops.hear: The tune in quick repeated notes, with solos for oboe and flute
The whole orchestra, loud, the tune now moving in flowing triplets
The opening notes once more, quietly, over darker chords and a held bass note

notice: The surprise happens only once. Listen to how Haydn keeps the later variations interesting without repeating the joke.
The coda sets the innocent tune against darker harmonies. It sounds thoughtful, almost wistful.

movements.heading: Menuet: Allegro molto
movements.summary: A [[minuet|minuet]] in name, but marked “very fast”. At this speed it is too quick to dance: it points towards the [[scherzo|scherzo]] that would later replace the minuet in symphonies.

stops.hear: A quick, sturdy dance for the full orchestra
The music becomes gentler and lighter
The sturdy dance returns

notice: Tap your foot to the beat. At this tempo you will feel one strong beat to a bar rather than three.

movements.heading: Finale: Allegro di molto
movements.summary: A fast, high-spirited finale that combines [[sonata-form|sonata form]] with a [[rondo|rondo]]: the opening tune keeps returning, even in the middle of the stormier passages. The timpani get the last word.

mainIdeas.name: The refrain
mainIdeas.description: a quick, lightweight tune in the violins that seems to run on tiptoe.

mainIdeas.name: The drums
mainIdeas.description: in the closing pages the timpani come to the front.

stops.hear: The violins dash off with a quick, light tune, quietly
The whole orchestra joins in, loudly
The tune breaks into fragments; the music turns to minor keys

stops.label: Mid-development
stops.hear: The opening tune peeks in, in the middle of the stormier music
stops.happening: A return of the refrain inside the development

stops.hear: The opening tune back in the home key

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: Loud drum rolls and strokes under the whole orchestra

notice: The drum that made the surprise in the slow movement returns at the end of the finale, now in the open.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Colin Davis made the recording in the Concertgebouw in Amsterdam, as part of his series of Haydn’s London symphonies with the orchestra.

threads.title: Quiet before loud
threads.body: Haydn often starts softly so that the full orchestra lands with more force: in the first movement, in the slow movement and in the finale.

threads.title: The timpani
threads.body: The drum stroke of the surprise returns as the leading voice at the end of the symphony.

threads.title: Simple tunes
threads.body: Every movement is built on tunes that are easy to sing, which is why the surprises in harmony and volume are so clear.
